key_insight: HiMuon speeds up Muon optimization by applying the same finite Newton-Schulz update independently to small tiles instead of coupling the entire weight matrix.
engineering_relevance: This makes optimizer updates much cheaper and more GPU-friendly, enabling tile-based kernels, batching, chunking, and runtime schedules for large neural-network training.
method: Split each momentum-gradient matrix into T×T tiles.
Run the finite Newton-Schulz map separately on each tile.
Reassemble tiled updates to form the full optimizer step.
evidence_signal: The paper reports transformer-training experiments and controlled matrix-function diagnostics showing improved step efficiency while staying close to full-matrix Muon in the tested settings.
watch_item: Because cross-tile spectral interactions are discarded, the tiled update is a local matrix-function approximation and may behave differently from full Muon for some matrix sizes or tile choices.
paper_title: Hierarchical Muon: Tiled Newton-Schulz Updates for Efficient Muon Optimization
